subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: One atom
hotspots.description: This whole structure — tiny nucleus, orbiting electrons, mostly empty space — is one single atom, the smallest particle of an element.
hotspots.positionHint: The nucleus and electron cloud together.
hotspots.function: Shows the complete structure of a single atom.

hotspots.label: The nucleus
hotspots.description: The tiny bundle at the center is the nucleus — protons and neutrons packed together, holding nearly all the atom's mass.
hotspots.positionHint: The small red-and-gray bundle at the center.
hotspots.function: Shows the dense core of the atom.

hotspots.label: The electron cloud
hotspots.description: The huge, mostly-empty region around the nucleus is where the electrons orbit — far outside the core, in mostly-empty space.
hotspots.positionHint: The large translucent sphere with electron dots.
hotspots.function: Shows the electrons orbiting far outside the nucleus.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. A single atom floats centered, lit with soft neutral studio light — no rim-light glow, no bloom, no emissive anywhere. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Nucleus: small soft red/gray bundle; electron cloud: large translucent warm-white shell with small teal electron dots; wide empty gap. Strong saturated color is reserved for the small flat hotspot dots (amber / coral / molecular-green accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere, single 2K shared texture atlas. Protons: soft muted red, roughness ~0.4. Neutrons: soft muted gray, roughness ~0.4. Electron dots: small muted teal, roughness ~0.4. Cloud shell: translucent warm-white, alpha ~0.1. No emissive channels anywhere — any glow is handled by app runtime UI.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: a single atom, built to be read as 'the tiny brick of everything — mostly empty space, dense nucleus, orbiting electrons.' Three procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: a ball-model atom — small nucleus bundle at center (a few soft red and gray spheres, radius ~0.28), a large translucent warm-white electron-cloud sphere (radius ~1.7, alpha ~0.1) with small muted teal electron dots (radius ~0.06) drifting on two shell rings, and a clear empty gap between nucleus and cloud.

2) BUILD A MOLECULE (toggleable layer): a second identical atom fades in to one side and eases toward the first; a soft shared-pair band appears between them (app-driven) — two atoms bonding into a molecule.

3) ZOOM (toggleable layer): the app animates the camera zooming in from a fingertip-scale object (a small finger-scale ball at cloud distance) down to the atomic scale, emphasizing how small atoms are.

Camera: framed so the whole atom fits with negative space; auto-rotate default. Budget 6-10k triangles. Named nodes: NucleusBundle, Protons, Neutrons, ElectronCloud, ElectronDots, ShellRing_01, ShellRing_02, PartnerAtom, SharedPairBand, FingertipScale. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer.
